faq: What does 'initial' mean in the name?

The bearing at the start of the route. A great-circle heading changes continuously as you travel, so a single bearing can only describe one point of it — this tool is precise about which point: the first.
Why is the result not exact at the destination too?

Because the arrival bearing differs — the same curve crosses the destination's meridian at its own angle. The reverse journey needs its own initial bearing, which this calculator gives when you swap the points.
The standard spherical initial-bearing formula: atan2 of sin Δλ·cos φ₂ against cos φ₁·sin φ₂ − sin φ₁·cos φ₂·cos Δλ, normalised to 0–360°. The guide on this page shows it in full.

Initial bearing or rhumb bearing for a short hop?
At short range they nearly coincide; the difference grows with distance and latitude. Ocean passages care; harbour hops do not.
Can it handle points across the antimeridian?
Yes — the formula works in longitude differences, and the shortest path across the Pacific is handled without a 360° surprise.
Is the result true or magnetic?
True (from geographic north). Apply local magnetic declination before using it with a magnetic compass.
